studies.Population: Prostate cancer cases and age-matched hospital controls in Japan

studies.Reference: A case-control study of diet and prostate cancer in Japan: possible protective effect of traditional Japanese diet.
studies.Authors: Sonoda T, Nagata Y, Mori M, Miyanaga N, Takashima N, Okumura K, Goto K, Naito S, Fujimoto K, Hirao Y, Takahashi A, Tsukamoto T, Fujioka T, Akaza H
studies.exposure_measurement_supporting_text: Average daily intake of food from 5 years before the diagnosis was measured by means of a semi-quantitative food frequency questionnaire.

sample_size.excerpt: We studied 140 cases and 140 individually age ( +/- 5 years)-matched hospital controls for analysis.
sample_size.location: Abstract, sentence 5; total_n derived from reported group counts 140 + 140 = 280

cases.excerpt: We studied 140 cases and 140 individually age ( +/- 5 years)-matched hospital controls for analysis.

effect_size.excerpt: first quartile and 95% confidence intervals (95%CIs) were 0.45 (0.20-1.02) for fish, 0.53 (0.24-1.14) for all soybean products, 0.47 (0.20-1.08) for tofu, and 0.25 (0.05-1.24) for natto. Consumption of fish and natto showed significantly decreasing linear trends for risk (P < 0.05).

confidence_interval.excerpt: first quartile and 95% confidence intervals (95%CIs) were 0.45 (0.20-1.02) for fish, 0.53 (0.24-1.14) for all soybean products, 0.47 (0.20-1.08) for tofu, and 0.25 (0.05-1.24) for natto.

p_value.excerpt: Consumption of fish and natto showed significantly decreasing linear trends for risk (P < 0.05).

comparison.excerpt: ORs of the fourth vs. first quartile and 95% confidence intervals (95%CIs) were 0.45 (0.20-1.02) for fish, 0.53 (0.24-1.14) for all soybean products, 0.47 (0.20-1.08) for tofu, and 0.25 (0.05-1.24) for natto.

design.excerpt: We performed a case-control study on dietary factors and prostate cancer in order to assess the hypothesis that the traditional Japanese diet reduces the risk of prostate cancer.

timing.excerpt: Average daily intake of food from 5 years before the diagnosis was measured by means of a semi-quantitative food frequency questionnaire.

continent.excerpt: Four geographical areas (Ibaraki, Fukuoka, Nara, and Hokkaido) of Japan were selected for the survey.

exposure_measurement.excerpt: Average daily intake of food from 5 years before the diagnosis was measured by means of a semi-quantitative food frequency questionnaire.
